title: Data Types
description: Discover the different shapes and sizes of treasures you can store in your magic boxes.

content.value: Remember our magic boxes (variables) from the last lesson? Well, you can't just put anything in them the exact same way. Think about your toy box: you have soft teddy bears, hard building blocks, and watery slime. They are all different kinds of toys!
In Python, we have different kinds of data too. Let's learn about the three most important ones: Integers, Floats, and Strings.
Integers are just normal, whole numbers. Like the number of apples you have, or your age. No dots or fractions allowed!
What if you have half a cookie? Or what if you are measuring your height? For that, we use 'Floats'. A Float is a number with a decimal point (a dot) in it.

Strings are used for words, names, and sentences. To make a string, you MUST wrap your words in quotation marks like a cozy blanket. If you forget the blanket, the computer will shiver and get confused!
You can use double quotes (") or single quotes ('). Both work perfectly fine as long as you use the same one at the beginning and the end.

editorCode:
apples = 5
cookies = 2.5
hero = "Spiderman"

print(apples)
